main_text.p: tinctas, quæ fale maceratis piscibus carni-bufq; admodum delectabantur, ac crebrius vescebantur. Certissimum est exta & viscera vitiari ac tabescere, oraq; cum anima grā-ue illius virus exhalare ex fallamentorum omnis generis immodico vfu. Ergo fal, qui defunctorum corpora per fecula a putrefa-ctione vindicat, viuentia corrumpit ac ene-cat.
Viri quia in exercitamentis sunt impigri-ores, lentius scorbuto inficiuntur. Qui novi orbis res literis mandarunt, aiunt Nigritas fale valetudinem tueri, & pene cum auro æquare.

Et tantum de fale, quod falso Arist. putant[?] frigore & humore diffolui, calido ac ficco cogi, cū calido & humido quoq; eliquefcat, nā raphano afperfus, aut fi raphani, q natura calidus est & humidus, fruita falis aceruo in-deris, fal totus liquescet. Vide Langium in epist. 28 Plura de falis natura, conficiendi illius ratione fingulari, vfu ac differentiis, tum etiam herbis quibusdam maritimis falfugi-nofo fuccoimbutis, & ex quibus fal elicitur, inueniet lector apud Lemnium l.3 de naturæ occult. mirac. c.9. Plin. l.31.c.7. & 9.

page.notes: The first digit of the page number is faint and read as 5 (long-s-like form). "putant" is uncertain: the word may be "putauit". The footnote lines after the text were read as foot notes in smaller type. The lowest-right "De" is the catchword. Heavy staining and show-through from the other side, mainly in the lower half, do not affect the reading of the main lines.
